$comment: The gauntlet: what 'the index works' actually means, in a file rather than in someone's memory. `rustgraph.py selftest` runs it and exits non-zero on any mismatch, and lint-index runs that -- which is also the only thing in CI that executes any Python at all. Expectations are deliberately about the TOP result, since that is what an agent acts on. When the README or the crates.io dump legitimately changes an answer, update the expectation in the same commit and say why.

queries.note: The list says Encoding and never serialization; this passes only via category term profiles.
Regression guard: clap's 1.1B downloads used to win this on fame alone.
README never says REST. Passes only via crates.io keywords; was NO ANCHOR before them.
Reached through the crates.io keyword 'orm', not the category name.
Was right by accident via AI/Genetic algorithms; keywords make it right via Concurrency.
Reached by keyword rarity: 'scraping' belongs to one crate here, while 'web' belongs to forty.

no_anchor.note: Must report no category match rather than dressing a guess as a ranking.

affinity.note: gRPC codegen; the highest-lift pair in the index and a check that lift is not just counting popularity.

runtime.note: Optional in Cargo.toml but inside the default closure; a plain optional flag would call this a free choice.
Genuinely runtime-agnostic: neither runtime is in its default closure.
